_readme: Risk gates for the shadow engine. Every value carries its own rationale, and
the whole file carries a version, because a threshold that can be changed
without changing a version cannot be audited after the fact.
These were set A PRIORI from the published fee schedule and the collector's
poll cadence - not fitted to any sample of decisions. Re-tuning them on the
same outcomes they will later be judged against is how a strategy is
invented rather than found, so a change here must bump `version` and be
basis: a priori: Polymarket published fee schedule + the collector's MEASURED per-token refresh cadence; never fitted to observed decisions

corrected_from.why: v1 was derived from an incorrect premise: it assumed the collector re-polled each book every 5s. Measuring the real archive (2026-10-11, 66 tokens, 387 observations over 13 minutes) gives a per-token refresh gap of min 11.1s, p50 37.9s, p90 157.3s - because the worker sweeps tokens sequentially under a 45s per-cycle budget. At 15s, more than half of a perfectly healthy book would be judged stale by construction, so the gate would have refused everything regardless of the market. This is a correction of a wrong measurement, not a relaxation in response to outcomes: no decision had been observed when it was made.

min_net_edge_usd_per_share.rationale: The weather taker fee peaks at 0.05 * 0.25 = 0.0125 per share at p=0.5, and the execution buffer adds 0.5% of notional (0.005 at p=1). A floor of 0.02 clears worst-case documented costs with 0.0025 to spare, before any claim about model skill. Below this the model has to be right more often than the fee schedule alone already eats.

max_snapshot_age_ms.rationale: Two collector sweeps. The measured per-token refresh gap is p50 37.9s (real archive, 2026-10-11) under a 45s per-cycle budget, so 90s admits the newest book the collector can produce while still refusing one that is two refreshes behind - which means that token is no longer being watched at all. Below one sweep (45s) the gate would fire on healthy books; a book older than 90s is not a live market, it is a record of a market we stopped watching.

max_forecast_age_hours.rationale: A run is publishable 12h after initialisation (single_runs PUBLISHABLE_LAG_HOURS) and runs issue every 6h, so a healthy engine sees runs aged 12-18h. 30h tolerates two missed cycles of upstream outage without admitting a run so old the lead-time bucket it prices has moved.

proposed_shares.rationale: Large enough that a thin book shows up as a partial fill rather than filling instantly and hiding its own emptiness; small enough that depth is never the binding constraint on a market that has any. Shadow only - no order is ever placed and no capital exists.

require_complete_fill.rationale: A partial fill is not a smaller trade, it is a different trade: the unfilled remainder would have to be repriced against a book we just drove through. Refusing it keeps every ACCEPT interpretable.

min_depth_usd.unit: USD notional on the traded side
min_depth_usd.rationale: A second, independent liquidity floor expressed in dollars rather than shares, so that a book resting entirely at 1c cannot pass a share-count check while being worth almost nothing.

max_decision_latency_ms.rationale: Reporting threshold only, not a gate. Above it the P95 latency metric flags the cycle as degraded so a slow evaluator is visible before it becomes an accuracy problem.
